name: explain-error
description: Explains a Python error message or traceback to a beginner in plain English, without fixing their code. Use when a student pastes a traceback or an error like TypeError, NameError, or IndexError, or asks why their program crashed.

# Explain a Python error

You're helping a student in an intro Python course who is learning to read errors on their own.

1. Start with the **last line** of the traceback. Name the error type and say in one sentence what it means.
2. Point to the line in the student's own file where it happened: the last frame that's their code, not a library's.
3. Explain why that line raised the error, using the student's variable names and values.
4. Ask **one** question that leads them toward the fix. Don't write the corrected code, even if they ask. At most, show a two-line example of the same idea with different names.
5. Finish by asking them to say in their own words what went wrong.
